custom.label: Change contraction words
custom.text:
Add a suggestion to change contractions to their full forms.
While writing a formal document, it is preferred to use a full form word instead of shorten/contracted form.
For example, instead of I'm, it should be I am; he's should be he is; didn't should be did not; can't should be cannot, etc.

custom.label: Capital letters for official names
custom.text:
Make sure every official name starts with a capital letter: people's names, brand and company names, universities and schools, organisations and government offices, cities, countries, languages and nationalities.
For example: universitas gadjah mada → Universitas Gadjah Mada, national taiwan university → National Taiwan University, samsung → Samsung, jakarta → Jakarta, english → English.
Fix every one you find, even in a document with good English; these fixes don't count toward the replacement budget.
Small words inside a name stay lower case (University of Indonesia), and acronyms and brands stay as they are officially written (NTU, iPhone).
Degree and field names stay lower case (bachelor's degree in chemistry); only official program names keep their capitals.

custom.label: Check for a document fully generated by AI
custom.text:
Judge whether the whole document was generated by AI and handed in without the student rewriting it. Look at the document as a whole: one polished sentence is not enough. Signs, strongest first:
1. Leftovers from the AI chat: notes to a proofreader or reviewer, "working draft", "revise into your own voice", a "Points to verify before submission" or checklist section, placeholders like [University Name], or the applicant called "the applicant" or "he/she" in their own document. Check the page header and footer in file_facts too.
2. The file facts say the file was made by a program that AI chat tools use (python-docx), and never edited in Word.
3. No real target: several universities named at once, or "this program" and "the university" never named.
4. Careful, legal-sounding hedges a student would not write: "if appropriate and feasible", "subject to the curriculum and course availability", "provided they comply with applicable regulations", "I do not intend to assume…", "rather than assuming…", "the objective is not to … but to …".
5. Everything general, nothing specific: no numbers, dates, results, names of projects, products, people or places they worked; experiences told as lists of skills.
6. Long lists of abstract nouns in one sentence (pricing, costs, customer preferences, presentation, sales channels, and business planning) and the same polished words again and again (meaningful, sustainable, commercially viable, valuable, align, bridge, foster, equip).
7. A template shape: numbered sections with headings like Background, Motivation, Why Taiwan, Why this program, Research direction, Beyond the classroom, Financial planning, Career goals; a research part with a working title "…: Perspectives from …", numbered research questions and a methodology; bullet points that each start with a bold phrase and a colon, all the same length; every paragraph opening with a topic sentence and closing with a summary; a last paragraph starting "Ultimately," that repeats everything.
8. Perfect grammar and punctuation with not a single typo.

When several of these signs appear across the document (always when there is a sign 1 or 2 together with 4 to 8):
- Add one end_note_items point in Karina's voice. Ask whether they made it with AI, name two or three things you noticed in the text (never mention file_facts or the program that made the file), and ask them to rewrite it in their own words with their own real experiences, details and numbers. For example: "TBH, this whole study plan looks AI generated: it still has the notes for the proofreader, it never says which university you are applying to, and there are no real details from your own experience. Did you make it with AI? Please rewrite it in your own words and add your real experiences (what you did, the results, numbers), because the committee wants to know you, not a template."
- Put " (this one looks like AI generated)" after the 1 to 3 most obvious passages, and " (remove this, this is not part of your study plan)" after AI chat leftovers (name the document type: study plan, autobiography…).
- Mention the program that made the file only in the private reason.
When only one or two passages sound generic, use the inline note for those passages only and do not add the end note.
